title: Constructive vs Classical IVT: Avoiding Classical Logic in Bisection
description: Answers the question: can the constructive IVT be proved without classical logic? YES for the structural bisection core — width bounds, sign preservation, and monotonicity are proved via a parameterized bisection (a computable `def`, not `noncomputable`) that takes explicit Bool choices instead of computing `if f(mid) ≤ 0`. NO for the exact root: endpoint convergence requires Classical.choice via completeness of ℝ. Identifies and formalizes the exact classical boundary.

meta.author: Lean Genius
meta.assumptions: None. Constructive core (Parts I-V) uses no classical axioms. Endpoint convergence (Part VI) uses Classical.choice via Mathlib's tendsto_atTop_ciSup (completeness of ℝ). Root theorem (Part VII) uses Continuous.tendsto.
originalContributions: paramBisect: computable (non-noncomputable) bisection parameterized by explicit choice oracle
paramBisect_width: exact width formula (b-a)/2^n for any choice sequence — no classical logic
paramBisect_sign: sign invariant f(left)≤0≤f(right) preserved given SignConsistent oracle — no classical logic
paramBisect_nested: interval nesting — later intervals contained in earlier ones
paramBisect_width_tendsto_zero: width→0 for any choice sequence
paramBisect_endpoints_converge: endpoints converge to common limit (classical, via tendsto_atTop_ciSup)
bisection_limit_is_root: limit is root when f continuous and choices sign-consistent
constructive_vs_classical_ivt: complete summary of constructive vs classical boundary

openQuestions.question: For functions with Decidable comparisons (e.g., polynomial sign over ℚ), does paramBisect give a fully computable IVT with no noncomputable components at all?
Can the exact IVT be proved in Lean using a constructive reals model (e.g., Cauchy reals with computable convergence rates), bypassing Classical.choice?

meta.proofStrategy: Separates the bisection algorithm into a computable part (structural theorems, proved without Classical.em) and a classical part (which branch to take, requires Classical.em). Proves the constructive core by induction using explicit Bool choice sequence. Classical convergence uses tendsto_atTop_ciSup and tendsto_atTop_ciInf from Mathlib.

sections.title: Computable Parameterized Bisection
sections.description: Defines paramBisect as a regular (computable) def that takes choices: ℕ → Bool instead of computing the branch decision from f.

sections.title: Width Bounds (Constructive)
sections.description: Proves the exact width formula (b-a)/2^n by induction, without classical logic.

sections.title: Ordering and Containment (Constructive)
sections.description: Proves left≤right, left-nondecreasing, right-nonincreasing, containment in [a,b], and interval nesting — all without classical logic.

sections.title: Sign Preservation (Constructive)
sections.description: Proves the sign invariant f(left_n)≤0≤f(right_n) holds when the choice sequence is sign-consistent — no classical logic.

sections.title: Width Convergence
sections.description: Proves width→0 using tendsto_const_nhds and tendsto_pow_atTop_nhds_zero_of_lt_one.

sections.title: Endpoint Convergence (Classical)
sections.description: Proves endpoints converge to a common limit using tendsto_atTop_ciSup and tendsto_atTop_ciInf — requires Classical.choice via completeness.

sections.title: Root Theorem (Classical)
sections.description: Proves the limit is a root of f when f is continuous and choices are sign-consistent — uses le_of_tendsto and ge_of_tendsto.

sections.title: Main Summary Theorem
sections.description: Assembles all results into constructive_vs_classical_ivt, a single theorem that precisely states which parts of bisection-based IVT are constructive and which require Classical.choice.

proven: Sign invariant preservation under explicit oracle — constructive
Endpoint convergence to common limit — classical
Root theorem for continuous f — classical
open: Fully computable IVT for Decidable f (no classical axioms at all)
knownResults.goal: Identify and formalize the exact classical boundary in constructive IVT proofs
